changelog:
[B][COLOR ff00fa9a]Version 2.0.27[/COLOR][/B]
[COLOR fffdb515]New: subtitles translated by Gemini[/COLOR]
-When neither the video nor the subtitle providers have a subtitle in your preferred language, luc_kodi takes one that exists in another language and Gemini translates it into yours (Spanish, Romanian, Italian or any language in Settings > Subtitles). English comes first as the source, then your secondary language and the languages of the tracks inside the file.
-Gemini translates in blocks of 50 lines with the lines before them as context, so sentences split across two lines and the tone between characters survive. Every line comes back in its place, with its italics and line breaks; Castilian and Latin American Spanish are two different languages.
-The source is chosen with care: the subtitle made for the exact file playing first, a person's work before a machine translation, and it is checked against the timing of the file before translating. If it cannot be downloaded, is a web page instead of a subtitle, or fits no timing, the next one is used (up to three).
-Long lines are split near their middle, and a line too long to read in time stays on screen a little longer, never into the next one. Starts never move.
-The translation runs in the background, up to five blocks at a time, and usually takes 15 to 30 seconds per episode. It stops if you stop or change video.
-One language at a time: your preferred language first and, only if that fails, your secondary language, from the same source and without downloading it again.
-Your Gemini keys are used in order: the first while it has quota, then the next. A model Google reports as overloaded, or that does not answer within 25 seconds, rests for two minutes and the next model translates. Empty answers, missing lines, names left unchanged and the few lines Google refuses to translate no longer throw a translation away.
-Each translation is kept on the device (the newest 40), so watching again costs nothing. Settings > Subtitles > Translate with Gemini AI (on by default; needs a Gemini key under Accounts (Meta) > Gemini AI), with Delete translated subtitles under it.
[COLOR fffdb515]New: SubtitleCat, a second subtitle provider[/COLOR]
-SubtitleCat (subtitlecat.com) joins OpenSubtitles: no account or key, and often new releases first. Settings > Subtitles > Subtitle providers has a switch for each: use one, the other or both.
-From SubtitleCat luc_kodi takes the file someone uploaded, in your language as it is or in another as the source for a translation. Its own line-by-line Google translations are only a last resort, and can be turned off.
-The original language is read from the site or from the subtitle's own text, and a result is only taken when its name starts with the title and, for an episode, says its SxxEyy.
-If OpenSubtitles cannot sign in or has used your daily downloads, SubtitleCat is asked instead.
[COLOR fffdb515]New: subtitles synced to the video[/COLOR]
-Most video files carry subtitle tracks, and their index says when each line starts (the cues of an MKV, the sample table of an MP4). luc_kodi reads that index, a few requests and nothing of the video, and moves every external subtitle onto it: shifted, and stretched when it was made for another frame rate. Only the times change, never the text.
-A remaster or another broadcast is often cut differently, so a subtitle can be right in one stretch and off in the next (a longer scene, a commercial break). Then it is fitted in stretches, up to five, each with its own shift; where each stretch starts is found the way the open-source aligner alass does it, line by line.
-A fit is only applied when it is clearly real: it must beat what wrong shifts and the same subtitle played backwards score against the file. A subtitle already in sync, or one that fits nothing, is left as it is.
-Blu-ray picture subtitles (PGS) are matched by when lines appear and disappear, text tracks are preferred because their times are exact, and commentary tracks are never used.
-When the OpenSubtitles subtitle picked by name fits no timing, the next ones in the same language (two at most, each is a download from your quota) are tried and the first that fits is loaded.
-The notification that says the subtitle is loaded also says how far it moved. Files without a subtitle track of their own (CAM, AVI, TS) keep the subtitle as it comes. Settings > Subtitles > Sync subtitles to the video automatically (on by default).
[COLOR fffdb515]Subtitles: better choices[/COLOR]
-OpenSubtitles subtitles uploaded for the exact file playing (found by its fingerprint: size and first and last 64 KB) come first.
-Releases that number a season differently from TMDB (Columbo season 10) got subtitles of another episode. When the file name carries the episode title, OpenSubtitles is also asked by that title and by the file's fingerprint, whatever number they were given.
-Your secondary subtitle language works for episodes too, its track inside the video first, and it is also tried when everything found in your preferred language had to be discarded. Subtitles chosen by luc_kodi are switched on.
-Broken letters (a subtitle saved in the wrong character set, or UTF-8 read twice) are repaired, for Romanian, Central European, Cyrillic, Greek and Turkish subtitles. A subtitle whose letters are lost for good is skipped for the next readable one.
-The same line shown twice at once (song lyrics in Korean dramas) is shown once.
-Episode subtitles named with the absolute episode number (Turkish series: "Kurulus Osman 168") are no longer thrown away, and subtitles are looked up in the background, so Skip Intro and tracking never wait for them.
[COLOR fffdb515]Playback: no more dead ends[/COLOR]
-Easynews web search: luc_kodi first asks for the end of the file, which Kodi needs before the first frame. If it does not arrive in time, the source is skipped instead of failing after 20 seconds, with a short notification: "This file is broken, playing the next one".
-Easynews + Newznab: a segment pointing at the wrong article no longer stops the episode after 30 seconds; it is treated like a missing article.
-Samples instead of the episode: a short video next to an archive many times its size, or named "sample", is no longer streamed as the release, and any source whose video lasts far less than the title (under 10 minutes and a quarter of the runtime) is skipped like a dead link.
-VC-1 video on Android devices whose only VC-1 decoder is the maker's own (Samsung: c2.sec.vc1.decoder) showed noise instead of the picture. Autoplay now skips it for the next source; one you pick yourself plays with a warning. NVIDIA Shield and other devices with a real VC-1 decoder are not affected.
[COLOR fffdb515]Gemini models up to date[/COLOR]
-Checked against Google's model list of November 2026: Gemini 3.7 Flash and 3.5 Flash are now answered by 3.8 Flash and 3.6 Flash, and gemini-2.5-flash shuts down on 1 December 2026, so they leave the fallback list and the model setting, and a stored choice moves to its replacement. The list is 3.5 Flash-Lite, 3.1 Flash-Lite, 3.6 Flash, 3.8 Flash and, for projects that still have it, 2.5 Flash-Lite.
[COLOR fffdb515]One look for every window[/COLOR]
-The side panels (context menu and its search, System status, Sync your devices, Usenet report) share the grey of the centred windows (Search, Rescrape options, the Assistant) instead of their own blue. Accent colours stay as they were.
[COLOR fffdb515]Fixes[/COLOR]
-A subtitle notification no longer appears two or three times in a row, or empty: notifications from the service and the plugin now take turns.
-When the next episode started while the previous one was still playing, it got no subtitle: the one on screen, loaded for the previous episode, was taken as already there.
